answer: Shared audit cost pool charges each new agent identity a $12 audit fee, refunded only after a random sample of its actions passes independent checks. An honest agent earns that fee back through a grove of repeat jobs, while a cloner must pay $12 per fake identity and risks losing the refund when its prism of duplicate behavior is detected. This makes cloning costlier than honesty because each fake island identity adds another $12 unrecoverable fee before any work is accepted.
